builds.note: vite build --minify false preserves function names for CPU attribution; both builds use the identical flags, React production mode and mocked data.

limitations: Browser cells run headless Chromium on the 2-vCPU task host through mocked /api/market responses; absolute milliseconds belong to this host, the paired delta is the result.

CPU budget functions come from a V8 sampling profiler at 200 us; they attribute self-time, not call counts. Native setData counts are exact in the module cells; the browser cells measure native cost end-to-end.

The camera for pan cells is driven by scripted mouse drags: baseline blocking coalesces pointer moves differently, so the exact final bar offset can differ (same page count, same 500-bar window). Pixel parity is claimed for the restore cells only.

The deferred restore burst shows the pre-burst window while pages load and the saved viewport after the single final apply + restore; the baseline shifted the logical range per page but the same bars stayed visible, so the intermediate images are equivalent.
WebSocket market updates are stubbed (no live ticks) in these cells; live indicator gating is covered by node:test, not by a live-feed browser cell.
The module work-count cells use counting series stubs, so they isolate JS derivation and count native calls without timing the library.
